identity: SHA256 of canonical complete history JSON; input quotas cannot be silently reduced on a failure or unknown decision.

quotas.construction: Choose CO and legal NoConflict visibility cuts, then generate real per-TX operations against those snapshots/own overlays.
Same construction with full CO prefix.

Change a read to another observed source identity on its key. For the first 50, choose a source write later in that same transaction's program order; remaining 100 choose any different known source. Keep every complete factual final-write order; do not select histories by any oracle result.
Append two consecutive reads of distinct known versions on one key.
Two writers of a fresh shared key both read its initializer before writing; noise does not touch that key.
Disjoint writer keys, all concurrent ring reads from initialization, with independently varying local operations.
A separate transaction reads the first of two writes by another confirmed committed writer; only the latter is its final version.

A constructed valid nonempty input, alternating maxStates=0 and maxSemanticChecks=0.

range.finalWriteOrders: Explicit and complete in every generated input, including expected-inconclusive source/budget cases.

programShapes: Require a distinct separate SHA after normalizing literal TX/key/version names to first-appearance TX/key and exact producer positions. This removes plain identity renaming but is not graph-isomorphism canonicalization. Do not present different transaction-array permutations as a proof of nonisomorphism. Retry only input-byte or shape duplicates before evaluation, at most 100000 generation attempts, and report all attempt/duplicate counts.
repeatedBusinessValues: Every third fixture additionally records a non-input businessValueFacts sidecar assigning one repeated payload to distinct version identities. The oracle checks tagged version/source states, not payload equality or an arbitrary-value SQL model; no identity may be merged because these payloads repeat.
frozenBeforeEvaluation: All original input JSON bytes and input SHA256
Per-input expected status or explicit exploratory null
evaluation: Run both SI and TOTALVIS controls without consulting graph-kernel outputs. Check every satisfiable certificate with the separate literal CO/VIS relation interpreter. Keep all unsatisfiable, unknown, invalid and mismatching outputs and classification counts; never regenerate to select a pass.
failurePolicy: Retain the first frozen dataset and original outputs/receipt before any correction. Fix implementation or record a separately justified expectation/generator issue; do not rewrite the original data.
